body: READ-ONLY REDUCER LOCALIZATION for the cand-70 blast; no Mote source edit. Current dirty Mote source at /Users/bbuchsbaum/code/rust/mote, base 2f38536, computes landability in src/state.rs around line 1533 by iterating every other candidate with the same landing repository and object format. That loop has no phase exclusion, so terminal Superseded cand-70 remains a mandatory exact pair for all pending rows. The reciprocal escape is structurally closed: src/reducer.rs around line 4605 rejects evidence updates unless the subject candidate is Pending. Existing candidate_protocol test hidden_pending_ancestor_blocks_until_superseded_by_descendant proves the successor itself becomes landable after supersession, but it already has predecessor pair evidence and does not include an unrelated third candidate; it therefore misses this incident. Minimal missing regression: make A landable; propose predecessor P and successor S; establish S contains/covers P; supersede P by S; assert A no longer needs a fresh pair with terminal P, while it still needs a current pair with live S. The narrow reducer remedy appears to be excluding Superseded and Abandoned candidates from the other-candidate pair loop, while retaining a deliberate decision for Landed and LandedOutOfBand rows rather than filtering blindly to Pending. Chief/Mote owner should decide and court that phase set. This would repair the 31-row terminal-predecessor blast without weakening pair checks among live candidates.
